description: Labeled QA set over the sample knowledge base (data/knowledge). 'relevant_sources' lists the source files that should be retrieved. Used to benchmark retrieval configurations and as reference data for Ragas.

items.question: What do enterprise buyers require before adopting an AI coding agent?
items.ground_truth: SOC2/ISO27001 compliance, no training on customer code, VPC/on-prem deployment, IP indemnification, SSO/RBAC and audit logs, and human-in-the-loop review before anything touches production.

items.question: What moats can a new entrant build in the AI coding-agent market?
items.ground_truth: Vertical depth in a domain, proprietary evaluation and reliability tooling, governance and workflow lock-in, and superior context engineering over the customer's codebase.

items.question: How is the AI coding-agent market segmented?
items.ground_truth: Into inline assistants (autocomplete/chat), agentic IDEs (a plan-apply-test loop over the workspace), and autonomous agents (asynchronous ticket-to-PR systems).

items.question: What weaknesses are common across AI coding-agent competitors?
items.ground_truth: Overclaiming autonomy relative to real reliability, weak handling of large messy legacy repositories, and thin observability into why an agent made a change.

items.question: What are the key risks for a startup entering this market?
items.ground_truth: Platform bundling risk from incumbents, model commoditisation eroding thin-wrapper moats, a reliability ceiling that erodes trust, and a heavy enterprise support burden.

items.question: Which SSO, SCIM and RBAC identity controls do enterprise buyers expect?
items.ground_truth: SSO and SCIM for provisioning, role-based access control, and per-repo permissions, alongside audit logs of who ran which agent.

items.question: How do per-seat versus usage-based pricing models affect enterprise budgets?
items.ground_truth: Per-seat pricing is predictable but caps upside; usage-based aligns cost to value but makes budgets unpredictable, creating procurement friction. A hybrid platform-fee-plus-usage model is emerging.

items.question: What role do design-partner programs play in go-to-market?
items.ground_truth: They co-develop governance features while doubling as product validation and a source of reference customers.

items.question: Why is a company that merely wraps a foundation model hard to defend over time?
items.ground_truth: If capability comes mostly from the foundation model, a thin wrapper has no defensible moat and is exposed to commoditisation and incumbent bundling.
